content.title: From The Masters to Memorial: Every tournament Scottie Scheffler has won
content.text: The World No.1 has 22 professional wins to his name, including four major championships.Scottie Scheffler is a prolific winner. Born in 1996, he has at least a decade left at the top of the game in which to add to his already impressive tally and secure his status as one of the best to play the game.The American made his PGA Tour debut as a 17-year-old at the HP Byron Nelson Championship in May 2014, four years before he turned pro. He made a hole-in-one during the third round and finished in a tie for 22nd place. Scheffler made his first major start in 2016, playing the US Open and leading after the first round, only to miss the cut after shooting a second-round 78. He won the low amateur prize the following year. The incredible amount Scheffler has won! What golf equipment does Scottie Scheffler use? Who is Scottie Scheffler’s wife? The Texan, who played for the Longhorns at the University of Texas at Austin, won his first professional tournament at the Evans Scholars Invitational on the Korn Ferry Tour in 2019. His first PGA Tour win came at the WM Phoenix Open in February 2022, and his first major title soon followed as he slipped on the coveted Green Jacket at The Masters in Augusta just two months later. Scottie Scheffler’s tournament wins in numbersIndividualPGA Tour 17DP World Tour 4Korn Ferry Tour 2Olympic Games 1TeamRyder Cup 1Presidents Cup 2Walker Cup 1Junior Ryder Cup 1Spirit International 1Scheffler has won a host of the PGA Tour’s biggest events, including the Players Championship, Arnold Palmer Invitational, The Memorial, and the Tour Championship, along with the FedEx Cup. He won his second Masters in 2024 and added his third at the PGA Championship in 2025, lifting the Wanamaker Trophy for the first time. That victory put him alongside Jack Nicklaus and Tiger Woods as the only men to win three majors and 15 PGA Tour titles before the age of 29. Scheffler – renowned for his unusual foot movement in his golf swing – is yet to win the other two men’s majors, but finished runner-up at the 2022 US Open at Brookline Country Club. His best finish at The Open Championship is a T7 at Royal Troon in 2024, but he leads the 153rd Open at Royal Portrush with little more than a round to to play. As well as success on the PGA Tour and in the Majors, Scheffler is an Olympic gold medalist having won the golf event in Paris in 2024. He’s also won both the Presidents Cup and Ryder Cup with the American team.Despite all of his success, Scheffler described golf as “an unsatisfying venture” during his pre-round press conference at the 2025 Open – he went on to win the tournament by 4-strokes over Harris English.Scottie Scheffler’s Achievements and AwardsKorn Ferry Tour Finals points list winner (2019)Korn Ferry Tour Player of the Year (2019)Korn Ferry Tour Rookie of the Year (2019)PGA Tour Rookie of the Year (2019-2020)PGA Tour Money List Winner (2021-2022, 2022-2023, 2023-2024)PGA Tour Player of the Year (2021-2022, 2022-2023, 2023-2024)Byron Nelson Award* (2022-2023, 2023-2024)Best Golf ESPY Award (2022-2023, 2023-2024)PGA Tour FedEx Cup (2024)*Given to the player with the lowest adjusted scoring average for the year in golf.**Presented to the professional golfer adjudged, irrespective of gender or nationality, to be the best in a given calendar year.Scheffler had topped the Official World Golf Rankings for 148 weeks as of July 14, 2025, and 113 consecutive weeks.
